newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, rally wanes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, rally wanes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday on light volumes, but the recovery in gold prices continued for a sixth day.
"There were no fireworks on the expiry of the March silver and gold options last Friday which may have disappointed some traders," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
"Silver and palladium have been the leaders lately with silver's fundamentals still positive, but the dollar and equity markets remain strong, keeping investors away from precious metals," he said.
COMEX April gold ended up 70 cents at $348.40 an ounce, after seeing a $347.40-349.10 intraday range. Total estimated gold futures volume was 37,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $345.00/50, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $346.25.

In the bullion market, implied gold lease rates have fallen sharply in the past few days, with the one month rate down to around 1.30 percent Wednesday from around 1.70 percent last Friday, suggesting short positions were being unwound, analysts said.

COMEX gold open interest fell a further 2,361 lots Tuesday, after a fall of 2,563 lots last Friday, suggesting the rally was being driven by fund shortcovering, traders said. COMEX was closed Monday for US Presidents Day.
COMEX gold stocks also continued to fall Tuesday, slipping 2,778 ounces to 602,361 ounces, the lowest level since October 1977.
"The physical market reportedly continues to be very tight, with strong demand from investors and jewellers for physical gold for prompt delivery," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
"Some producers have also been holding back from the market at recent lows, which further tightened supplies."
Spot gold saw three year lows around $336.40 an ounce last week.
The spot gold/silver ratio edged back up to 66.73 Wednesday, as gold began to catch up with silver's recovery, after the ratio saw a 22 month low last week.
COMEX March silver ended down 3.0 cents at $5.185 an ounce, after seeing a $5.225-5.155 intraday range.
Spot silver saw a six month high last week.

But both a standard five day slow stochastic oscillator and a nine-day relative strength indicator have climbed into overbought zones in the past few days, suggesting the silver market needed to digest its sharp gains of the past few weeks, before further advances are seen, traders said.

COMEX silver open interest rose for the second day in a row Wednesday, suggesting funds were building on their small net long positions, revealed in the CFTC Commitments of Traders data for the period ended February 11, released last Friday, analysts said.
Gold was slightly stronger than platinum also Wednesday, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread slipping to $22.10 an ounce, from $23.70 Tuesday.
NYMEX April platinum ended down $1.80 at $369.60 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed unchanged at $137.00.
In news Wednesday, Russia parliament's lower house approved government financial support for troubled Norilsk Nickel metals group which produces palladium, platinum and nickel.
Norilsk workers had given government until February 20 to pay off wage arrears. --Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641;
